advice: Telnet sends everything, including passwords, in plaintext. Disable it on the router/device or block WAN access immediately.
title: Telnet is exposed

advice: RDP is one of the most attacked services on the internet. Do not expose it directly; use a VPN or a jump host instead.
title: Windows Remote Desktop is exposed

advice: Databases should never face the internet from a home network. Bind it to localhost/LAN only, or reach it through a tunnel.
title: A database port (MySQL) is exposed

advice: Databases should never face the internet from a home network. Bind it to localhost/LAN only, or reach it through a tunnel.
title: A database port (PostgreSQL) is exposed

advice: Redis historically ships without authentication and is actively exploited when exposed. Bind to localhost/LAN only.
title: Redis is exposed

advice: Exposed MongoDB instances are routinely ransomed. Bind to localhost/LAN only and require authentication.
title: MongoDB is exposed

advice: Exposed memcached is abused for UDP amplification attacks and data leaks. Bind to localhost/LAN only.
title: memcached is exposed

advice: Port 7547 on a home gateway has a history of mass exploitation. This is normally your ISP's management channel — you usually cannot close it yourself; confirm with your ISP and make sure the modem firmware is current.
title: A router management protocol (TR-069/CWMP) is exposed

advice: An exposed Docker API is full remote control of the host. Bind it to localhost or a unix socket, never the WAN.
title: The Docker API is exposed without TLS

advice: Common and sometimes intentional, but it will be password-guessed around the clock. Prefer key-only auth, disable password login, or put it behind a VPN.
title: SSH is reachable from the internet

advice: FTP sends credentials in plaintext. Prefer SFTP (over SSH) or a modern file-sharing service.
title: FTP is exposed

advice: VNC authentication is weak and often password-only. Reach it through a VPN or SSH tunnel instead.
title: VNC remote desktop is exposed

advice: Exposed SMB has been the entry point for worms and ransomware (EternalBlue). Never expose SMB to the internet.
title: SMB file sharing is exposed

advice: Legacy Windows networking that should stay on the LAN. Check for an unintended port forward or UPnP mapping.
title: NetBIOS is exposed

advice: SNMP with default community strings leaks a full device inventory. Disable WAN-side SNMP or restrict it to your management network.
title: SNMP is exposed

advice: An open resolver at home is abused for amplification attacks and may violate your ISP's terms. Unless you deliberately run one, find the forward or UPnP mapping that opened it.
title: A DNS server is reachable from the internet

advice: Check what this is (banner/title in the report). If it is a router, NAS or camera login page, it should not be WAN-facing — and never over plaintext HTTP.
title: A web interface is reachable over plain HTTP

advice: Check the certificate and title in the report to identify it. Deliberate services are fine; an unfamiliar login page deserves a closer look.
title: A web service is reachable over HTTPS

advice: Alternate web ports often belong to device admin panels or dev servers that were never meant to be public. Identify it from the title/banner and close the forward if it is not deliberate.
title: A web interface is reachable on 8080

advice: Frequently a router or appliance admin panel. Confirm it is deliberate and its firmware is current.
title: A web service is reachable on 8443

advice: Winbox has a history of serious vulnerabilities. Restrict management to LAN/VPN and keep RouterOS current.
title: MikroTik Winbox management is exposed

advice: PPTP's encryption is considered broken. Migrate to WireGuard, OpenVPN or IKEv2.
title: A PPTP VPN endpoint is exposed

advice: Usually deliberate — this is the recommended way to reach home. Keep the server and certificates current.
title: An OpenVPN endpoint is reachable

advice: Usually deliberate — this is the recommended way to reach home. WireGuard does not respond to unauthenticated probes, so an 'open' result here can also be a false positive from UDP handling.
title: A WireGuard endpoint is reachable

advice: Deliberate if you use Plex remotely. Keep Plex updated; disable remote access in Plex settings if you do not use it.
title: Plex remote access is enabled

advice: If this is a Synology NAS, its admin interface should not be plain-HTTP on the WAN. Use HTTPS (5001), a VPN, or QuickConnect instead.
title: A service is reachable on 5000 (Synology DSM default)

advice: NAS login pages are high-value targets. Prefer VPN access; if it must be public, enable 2FA and keep DSM updated.
title: A Synology NAS interface is reachable

advice: NFS trusts client addresses and belongs on the LAN only. Remove the forward or UPnP mapping that exposed it.
title: NFS file sharing is exposed

advice: Unauthenticated rsync shares are a classic data leak. Restrict to LAN or tunnel it over SSH.
title: An rsync daemon is exposed

advice: Running mail from a residential connection is unusual and often against ISP terms; open relays are abused for spam. If this is not deliberate, find what opened it.
title: A mail server port is reachable
